body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 9dda297bd8b274d1677f9b9595e920507e9cc676 -->

**Verdict: Ready for a maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**

- PR #1686 intended the new reading. Its body says: "Closed inward STL and OBJ bodies turn outward at import." It merged with its own pins and its decision entry. The old test still expected the refusal from before #1686. Updating the test is the right fix. This PR hides no regression.
- The `#[test]` count in `crates/app/tests/winding_align.rs` stays at 9. One test is renamed. None is deleted.
- The new test says which side turns: `BodyWinding::Outward`. It also pins one import note, `load_model` equals `load_model_graded`, and the top face lays with a half turn. The note assert checks "1 closed solid(s) wound inward" and "12 facet(s) reversed". No assert is a tautology.
- The refusals stay pinned by name: `an_inside_out_cube_refuses_the_face_lay_by_name`, `an_inside_out_cube_refuses_the_321_by_name`, `bodies_are_judged_one_by_one`, and the nested-shell import refusals in `crates/app/tests/import_outward.rs`. All exist at this head.
- The note strings match the product format in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_outward.rs:43`.
- `docs/decisions/1752-inside-out-fixture-test.md` follows the format in `docs/decisions/README.md`: a `## #1752 - <title>` heading, Chosen, Why, Kept, Dropped.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` is added outside test functions. The new `.expect()` lines sit inside the renamed test function, like the existing fixture loads in this suite.
- The PR body is complete: what changed, how it was tested, what was not exercised, `Changelog: none`, and `Fixes #1752` at the end. The keyword closes issue #1752 when this merges. The subject is conventional: `test(import): ...`. One commit.

**Results**

Built on the self-hosted runner (macOS m3; the Linux runner is offline): https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43657275643 - conclusion success. Main sha in the run: `e2f012e9`.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Head check (the run tested `9dda297bd`) | pass |
| Trial merge with main `e2f012e9` | clean |
| Quick gate, `app:winding_align` whole suite | 9 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (37 s, 1 step, 0 failed) |
| Clippy, `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The run waited in the queue about 30 minutes behind another PR's run on the same runner. It was not cancelled.

The PR-review law changed during this review: builds must not depend on pr-test runs. The touched suite was therefore also run locally, merged with the newer main `25121045b`, in a review worktree:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Trial merge with main `25121045b` | clean, no conflicts |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test winding_align` | 9 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (incl. `the_inside_out_stl_fixture_is_turned_outward_at_import_and_lays ... ok`) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean, exit 0 |

**Requested before merge**

None.

**Notes**

- Main stays red until this merges. The cause is that PR #1686's quick gate did not run `winding_align`. That gap is separate owed work, not a blocker here.
- The other app suites and the batch tier were not run for this review. The post-merge gate runs them after the merge.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- review-cost: 9dda297bd8b274d1677f9b9595e920507e9cc676 -->

**Estimated agent cost:** ~$0.49 (88k tokens, estimate)

Model: session default. Route: local full-suite review (SlaveSession). A parallel clean review landed at 00:57Z and the PR merged before this review posted.

Blended upper estimate at list price; cache reads make the real cost lower.
